page: Amazon Web Services i4i.large is a storage-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8375C processor. This x86_64 architecture server features 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, and features a bundled 468 GB local NVMe SSD. The instance also provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the i4i.large delivers average single-core capabilities, as shown by its stress-ng single-core score of 1880.58 and Geekbench single-core score of 1558.0. However, because it is configured with only a single physical core, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth is also relatively low, measuring 14.18 GB/sec for large block reads and 13.19 GB/sec for large block writes. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, while static web serving throughput reaches 3.59 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i4i.large serves as a resource-dense entry point for workloads requiring fast local storage without the overhead of larger instance sizes. The primary tradeoff is the constrained compute and memory bandwidth, which limits its suitability for heavy parallel processing or high-throughput database operations. It is best suited for lightweight transactional databases, local caching layers, and low-concurrency storage-bound applications that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation and direct NVMe storage.
